title: The hazelnut
hook: Julian is shown all that is made as small as a hazelnut, kept because God loves it

segments.voice: Yesterday, Julian the anchoress, in her cell beside the church. Your line was all shall be well. Did you say it to a worry? Today, one more of her showings. Day eight hundred twenty-three.

Hold out one hand, palm up. Empty. Now set something very small in it in your mind: a bead, a seed, a nut. Something you could lose in a coat pocket and never notice. Julian of Norwich, the anchoress we met yesterday, says that in one of her showings God put a thing like that in the palm of her hand. Round as a ball. Small enough to close her fingers over. And when she asked what it was, an answer came. Today's showing fits in your hand: the hazelnut.
screen: `AN EMPTY PALM.` → `SOMETHING ROUND AND SMALL.` → `WHAT IS IT?`

segments.voice: First, the thing in her hand. In Grace Warrack's translation, Julian says she was shown "a little thing, the quantity of an hazel-nut, in the palm of my hand." She looked at it with what she calls the eye of her understanding, and wondered what it could be. The answer came: "It is all that is made." Everything. All of it, in a shape small enough to hold. Second, her fear. Julian wonders how it can last at all. It is so small, she thinks, that it might suddenly fall into nothing. That's an honest worry, and an old one: the world can feel that fragile. Third, the answer. She is told that it lasts, and always will, because God loves it. Not because it's strong. Not because it's large or useful or earned it. It is kept because it is loved. Fourth, what she sees in it. Julian says she saw three things in this little thing: that God made it, that God loves it, and that God keeps it. Made, loved, kept. She doesn't treat this as a lesson about the universe only. She goes straight on to speak of us, and of why we look for rest in things so small. For her, it's the same promise as all shall be well, made small enough to carry.
screen: `A LITTLE THING IN HER PALM.` · `IT IS ALL THAT IS MADE.` · `SO SMALL IT MIGHT FALL TO NOTHING.` · `MADE, LOVED, KEPT.` · then, large: `KEPT BECAUSE LOVED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold something small in your palm. A nut, a stone, a button, a coin, whatever is near. Rest your hand open on your knee with the thing in it. Look at it the way Julian did, with attention, not hurry. Notice how small it is, and how easily it could roll away. Then let it stand, for a moment, for everything: the world, the people you love, yourself. If you pray, you can hold her three words, made, loved, kept. If you don't, just keep the hand open and steady. The bell holds the time.
The hazelnut. Julian's showing of all that is made, small enough to sit in her palm, and lasting because God loves it. Today's word.
Your line: kept because loved. Today, carry the small thing from the practice in your pocket, and each time your hand finds it, remember Julian's answer. Day eight hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: Catholics who pray with Julian's Revelations of Divine Love return to the hazelnut passage in retreats and spiritual reading, and some keep a small stone or nut as a reminder of it.

notes: Confirm the exact Warrack 1901 wording of the two short quotations from chapter 5 ('a little thing, the quantity of an hazel-nut, in the palm of my hand'; 'It is all that is made.').

Paraphrased from chapter 5: 'round as a ball', 'the eye of my understanding', her marveling how it might last, the answer that it lasts because God loves it, and the three properties (made, loved, kept). Confirm.
howItsDone: 'some keep a hazelnut or small stone' is a general devotional description; soften or cut if not supported.

Audit (catholic 817-826): removed the narrator's own conclusion that the listener ('the person reading her book') is held by love; replaced with what chapter 5 goes on to say (we seek rest in things so little). Confirm against Warrack ch. 5.

Editor pass: trimmed the narrator's added list ('every person who has ever lived'), which Julian's text does not give; removed 'startling' (telling the listener how to react) and 'often' in howItsDone.
